statement_verbatim:
statement: >-
  Every endpoint declared by an htmx verb attribute (`hx-get`, `hx-post`, `hx-put`, `hx-patch`, `hx-
  delete`) MUST be exercised by at least one test. Bun/htmx realization mirroring
  `tester.convex.flow-router-route-coverage`; the declaration source differs, and that difference IS the
  adaptation — a Convex route is declared in `plan/_user_system_flows/_flow_routers/**/*.yaml`, an htmx endpoint is
  declared in the MARKUP, so the markup is this stack's route space.

statement: 'A journey spec (a `*.e2e.ts` file, or any test file whose header comments carry a `// UserSystemFlow:`, `// Journey:`
  or `// URN: test:userSystemFlow|journey:` marker) MUST carry exactly one binding header: `// UserSystemFlow: user-system-flow:<subject>:<slug>`
  or `// Journey: journey:<id>`, each matching the planner''s identity grammar. Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.journey-user-system-flow-header`,
  strict.'

statement: 'A journey spec MUST carry `// Layer: assembly`. Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.journey-layer-assembly`,
  strict.'

statement: A journey spec, meaning a browser spec (a `*.e2e.*` file, or a Playwright file bound to a user/system flow or journey), MUST NOT carry `// Acceptance:` or `// DESIRED_OUTCOME:` header lines; a bun test file is never a journey spec. Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.journey-no-acceptance-marker`,
  strict.

statement: A journey spec MUST carry at least one test URN `test:{userSystemFlow|journey}:<id>:{E2E|SMOKE|A11Y|VIS|RESP}-NNN-<slug>`,
  and every URN it carries MUST be well-formed and name the subject its binding header declares. Bun/htmx realization
  of `tester.vite.journey-urn-format`, strict.

statement: >-
  A test whose Phase is RED MUST assert behaviour; a case whose assertions are all existence checks
  (`toBeDefined` / `toBeTruthy` / `toBeFalsy` / `toBeNull` / `toBeUndefined`), or which asserts nothing at
  all, is refused. Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific detector over `bun:test` matchers. Realized by
  `bun_tester_discipline_detector`.

statement: >-
  A test whose Phase is RED MUST contain at least one guaranteed-fail marker. Accepted markers,
  transcribed from CORE `red.convention.yaml` -> `red_patterns.typescript`: `throw new Error('Not
  implemented …')`, `throw new UnimplementedError(…)`, `expect(false).toBe(true)`,
  `expect(true).toBe(false)`, `expect.fail(…)`, `return Promise.reject(…)`, and `it.fails(` /
  `test.failing(`. Bun realization of core `tester.red.test-must-fail-first`, mirroring
  `tester.convex.red-fails-first` rule for rule.

statement: 'A spec identified as responsive (a `RESP` test URN, or a `responsive`/`resp` token in its file name)
  MUST render the page at every viewport width declared in `atdd-bun.yaml` under `frontend.viewports` (default 375,
  768, 1280), through `page.setViewportSize({ width })`, a `viewport: { width }` option, or a list of widths it
  iterates (`for (const w of [...])`, `LIST.forEach`, `LIST.map`); picking one element of a list renders one width.
  It MUST pass `scrollWidth`, directly or through a variable measured from it, to an `expect(...)` so the test fails
  when the page overflows horizontally. New in the Bun/htmx browser tester, strict.'

statement: Every journey whose entrypoint is exposed and whose `surfaces` include `frontend` (or declare none) MUST
  have a journey spec bound to it by `// Journey:` with a RESP test URN. New in the Bun/htmx browser tester, strict.

statement: >-
  A test file that declares a `// Runtime:` MUST name a runtime in the JS/TS family (`bun`, `browser`,
  `isomorphic`, `typescript`, `ts`, `node`, `js`, `javascript`, `deno`, `vite`, `astro`, `preact`). Bun
  realization mirroring `tester.convex.routing-path`, which makes the same argument for Vitest.

statement: >-
  A test identified as a security test by its URN kind segment (`-SEC-`, `-RLS-`, `-AUTH-`) MUST contain
  an authentication/authorisation assertion — an expectation tied to 401, 403, unauthorised, forbidden,
  denied, permission, `.rejects` or `toThrow`. Bun realization of core `tester.security.auth`, mirroring
  `tester.convex.security-auth`.

statement: >-
  A test identified as an input-validation test by its URN kind segment (`-INPUT-`, `-VALIDATION-`,
  `-VALIDATE-`) MUST contain a rejection assertion — `.rejects`, `toThrow`, 400, 422, invalid, reject, or
  an error expectation. Bun realization of core `tester.security.input`, mirroring
  `tester.convex.security-input`.

statement: >-
  A test whose Phase is SMOKE MUST NOT substitute a production collaborator — `mock.module`, `spyOn`,
  `jest.mock`/`spyOn`, `vi.mock`/`spyOn`. Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific substitution vocabulary
  (`bun:test` exposes `mock` and `spyOn` where pytest uses `monkeypatch`). Realized by
  `bun_tester_discipline_detector`.

statement: >-
  A test whose Phase is SMOKE MUST assert on an operator-observable channel — HTTP response status or
  body, rendered markup, stdout/stderr, exit code — and not only on objects the test constructed itself.
  Stack-neutral obligation, Bun/htmx-specific channel vocabulary. Realized by
  `bun_tester_discipline_detector`.

statement: Every `.tsx`/`.jsx` component under a `presentation/` path segment MUST be covered by a SMOKE browser
  spec whose path names the component's product capability (the segment before `presentation`). Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.presentation-smoke-coverage`,
  strict.

statement: >-
  A telemetry test contains an assertion on the emission itself — `toHaveBeenCalled[With|Times]`, or
  an expectation on `.emit` / `.emitted` / `.capture` / `.track` / `.record` (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  A test identified as a telemetry test by its URN kind segment (`-TELEMETRY-`, `-EVENT-`, `-METRIC-`) or
  by `*.telemetry.test.*` colocation MUST contain an emission assertion — `toHaveBeenCalled[With|Times]`,
  or an expectation on `.emit` / `.emitted` / `.capture` / `.track` / `.record`. Bun realization of core
  `tester.telemetry.emit`, mirroring `tester.convex.telemetry-emit`.

statement: >-
  Every concrete telemetry URN a telemetry test claims in its `// Telemetry:` header appears in
  the test's code as an assertion string; a telemetry test with no header asserts at least one
  concrete telemetry URN (REQUIRED).
